articles.body:
Radio 5 Live , · 12 Sep 2026 , · 14 mins

In this week’s edition of The Football Interview, Kelly Somers speaks to Manchester City defender Rúben Dias. They discuss the transition into life under Enzo Maresca, after a decade of success with Pep Guardiola at the helm. They also get into how things have changed with Bernardo Silva and John Stones leaving over the summer. He reflects on the impact on his parents early on in his success to becoming one of the greatest central defenders in the world. articles.title: 14 of the Best Food Cities in the U.S. for Incredible Diversity and American Classics
articles.summary: From coast to coast, these are the destinations foodies love to visit.
articles.body:
In New York, complement your Michelin-starred restaurant experiences with top-notch dumplings and pizza.

With its Native American and Mexican culinary roots, Tucson, Arizona, was the first UNESCO City of Gastronomy in the U.S.

Start your Maine road trip in Portland and tuck into buttery lobster rolls and briny oysters.

Detroit is so multicultural, you'll find everything from Burundian food to tamales alongside the city's signature crispy square pizza.

Fusion fare abounds in Houston, where you can taste Viet-Cajun dishes or Southeast Asian-Latin American cuisine.

Calling all stateside gourmands: The United States is home to some truly incredible food cities. Fold a New York slice, pick up a pierogi, or bite into a Korean barbecue taco, and it's clear that U.S. gastronomy has benefited enormously from migration. In other words, the diversity of food across the country is unparalleled. In big cities like New York and San Francisco, and unexpected spots like Greenville, South Carolina, and Tucson, Arizona, there are hidden gems, lauded hot spots, and everything in between.

If you're traveling within the U.S. and you love to eat, here are 14 of the best foodie destinations across the country.

Some would argue New York City is the food capital of the U.S.; it's a melting pot of cultures with incredible culinary diversity, which means you can enjoy any type of cuisine here, from authentic dim sum at Joe's Shanghai in Manhattan's Chinatown to mouthwatering bagels with a schmear or meat-piled sandwiches at one of the city's dozens of Jewish delis like Katz's .

Don't confine yourself to Manhattan, either: Feast your way through the five boroughs, including stops in Astoria and Jackson Heights (in Queens) for authentic Greek and Himalayan fare, respectively. Brooklyn's Greenpoint neighborhood is home to a slew of Polish bakeries like Syrena , while Arthur Avenue in the Bronx and restaurants across Staten Island offer some of the city's best Italian food.

The Big Apple boasts dozens of Michelin-starred restaurants, ranging from fine-dining establishments like Le Bernardin to cool but low-key haunts like Jeju Noodle Bar . Don't get caught up in all things Michelin, though; no trip to New York would be complete without a slice of pizza at Williamsburg Pizza or L'Industrie .

Tucson was the first U.S. city to be deemed a UNESCO City of Gastronomy in 2015. Today, the destination continues to wow culinary connoisseurs with its unique offerings informed by Native American and Mexican traditions. The best Tucson restaurants incorporate locally sourced ingredients into their drinks and dishes. With this in mind, prickly pear margaritas are a staple here, as are nopales (edible cacti). Tucson's vibrant downtown district has bars and restaurants like Bata , which offers a largely veggie-focused menu, and the taqueria Boca , famous for its flavorful tacos and salsa flights.

Portland packs an outsized punch when it comes to food, with crowd-drawing restaurants serving everything from the iconic Maine lobster roll to pork belly yakitori. The city's small size makes it easy to cover a lot of ground. Even if you only have 24 hours in Portland before starting a road trip up the coast of Maine to visit Acadia National Park , you'll be able to get in multiple excellent meals and snack breaks. Start the day at Katie Made Bakery , a favorite for breakfast sandwiches, followed by lunch at perennial favorite Eventide Oyster Co ., which boasts more than a dozen oyster varieties and a top-notch lobster roll. For dinner, reserve (way) in advance at seasonal New American restaurant Fore Street , whose menu changes daily.

A road trip is a great way to discover regional specialties and hunt for hidden gems located beyond the city limits.

Wonderfully multicultural Detroit flexes its diversity, with the city's best restaurants ranging from James Beard Award-nominated Baobab Fare (East African cuisine) to Tamaleria Nuevo Leon and El Parian taco truck. For sushi, head straight to the sushi bar at beloved Japanese supermarket Noble Fish, located 20 minutes away in Clawson, Michigan. No trip would be complete without Detroit-style pizza—the square pies were originally baked in the steel pans used by auto workers and are still done the same way. The result is a tall but airy slice, with a very crispy crust. Order one at Grandma Bob's , Michigan & Trumbull , or nearby Pie Sci .

As one of America's most diverse hubs, it's no surprise that Houston made our list of the best U.S. cities for foodies. The Bayou City offers something for every palate. As such, options abound, like Viet-Cajun fusion at Crawfish & Noodles .

Another one of our favorites is ChópnBlok for its West African fare. We'd also be remiss not to highlight Houston's food truck scene, including the award-winning Coreanos , where diners can feast on Korean-Mexican fusion like Korean barbecue tacos.

Chicago is a foodie city, and Chicagoans are most passionate about their deep-dish pizzas and their unique ketchup-free hot dogs. The former and the latter are best enjoyed at Windy City staples Pequod's and Jimmy's Red Hots , respectively. Chicago also boasts over 50 James Beard Award winners and 19 Michelin-star-awarded restaurants, including the world-famous Alinea , best known for its creative multicourse tasting menus. Also consider the 33,000-square-foot City Winery Chicago (one part winery, one part restaurant, and one part bar and events space) and the 17,000-square-foot Kindling , a live-fire show kitchen helmed by James Beard Award winner Jonathon Sawyer.

Dining in New Orleans is a direct reflection of the city's diverse cultural influences from Europe, the Caribbean, and West Africa. With this in mind, the Big Easy should be, well, big on flavor. Savory staples here include po'boys from local fave Sammy's , jambalaya from Mother's , gumbo by the Gumbo Shop , crawfish étouffée by Creole House , and muffuletta sandwiches fresh from Verti Marte , which is open 24/7—all best paired with live jazz. Be sure to save room for powdered sugar-covered beignets at Cafe du Monde (yes, there will be a line, but it's worth it) and wash everything down with NOLA's most iconic cocktail, the Sazerac, at The Sazerac Bar at The Roosevelt New Orleans, A Waldorf Astoria Hotel.

In San Francisco , diners can indulge in meals at 29 Michelin-starred eateries, such as Atelier Crenn , where haute French cuisine is served in a swanky space; Mister Jiu's, featuring contemporary Chinese-American fare; and Lazy Bear , which bills itself as a "modern American dinner party."

Alternatively, for something more casual, make your way to the Ferry Building Marketplace , which is teeming with locally loved food vendors like Acme Bread Company, Dandelion Chocolate, El Porteño Empanadas, and Hog Island Oyster Company. Lastly, no trip to San Fran is complete without sampling some sourdough—both Josey Baker Bread and Boudin Bakery make some of the best in town. For namesake Mission burritos, locals and travelers alike love Taqueria Cancún .

This diverse Midwestern city has a seriously underrated and eclectic food scene fueled by nearby farms, local producers, and trailblazing chefs. For a taste of Cleveland's best eats, head straight to West Side Market , an indoor-outdoor market that offers something for everyone. Local vendors include Orale! Contemporary Mexican Cuisine, Pierogi Palace, Frank's Bratwurst, Theresa's Bakery, and Crepes de Luxe.

Then, carve out an afternoon to embark on your very own food tour of the city, including dim sum in AsiaTown and more pierogies in Slavic Village . The Land also has an incredible selection of Black-owned and Black-led restaurants like Pearl's Kitchen for top-notch comfort food, Yonder for delectable brunch, and Cleveland Cold Brew for coffee and pastries. Don't miss some of the city's more recent spots like Cordelia , which serves comfort food with a nostalgia-inducing Midwestern twist, and The Judith , a cozy Parisian-inspired cafe.

While Louisville is best known for its bourbon, you won't want to sleep on its exciting food scene. Boasting several award-winning chefs, the city is sure to delight food and drink enthusiasts alike. Hit the Urban Bourbon Trail , which highlights Louisville's best bourbon bars and restaurants—over 40 of them. While it may be tricky to hit the whole trail, must-visit spots include Jockey Silks Bourbon Bar , Merle's Whiskey Kitchen , and Doc Crow's Southern Smokehouse & Raw Bar . Finally, you can't leave Louisville without trying the city's signature dish, the Hot Brown. This delicious open-face sandwich—which features turkey, bacon, tomatoes, and Mornay sauce smothered on Texas toast—dates back to the 1920s when it was first invented at the Brown Hotel .

The Greenville that was a quiet cotton mill town is long gone; the city today is vibrant and full of unique culinary offerings rivaling larger nearby locales like Charlotte and Asheville. Here, you'll find Camp , which offers an eccentric menu featuring unique dishes like Thai-inspired calamari and lamb smothered in curry cream. For fresh seafood, try Coral or Jones Oyster Co. before snagging an afternoon pick-me-up at Methodical Coffee . Other must-visit spots include Scoundrel , a fantastic French brasserie headlined by acclaimed chef and Greenville native Joe Cash; farm-to-table fan-favorite Topsoil Kitchen & Market; and Mexican eatery Comal 864 .

Philly gives New York a run for its money when it comes to East Coast foodie cities. The humble cheesesteak is a Philadelphia icon; try an oxtail version at Taste Cheesesteak Bar in Center City, Joe's Steaks + Soda Shop in Fishtown, or Sonny's Famous Steaks in Old City. Lots of James Beard Award winners call Philadelphia home: Fishtown Thai hot spot Kalaya , Friday Saturday Sunday , an ultra-popular New American restaurant in Rittenhouse Square, and Vietnam Restaurant in Chinatown/University City. For an exceptional plant-based meal, head to Pietramala in Northern Liberties, which is BYOB and serves grilled oyster mushrooms with sweet corn and smoked eggplant with harissa, dukkah, and red lentils.

When you go to Los Angeles, you are surrounded by good Mexican food. The Pew Research Center even found that 30 percent of California's Mexican restaurants are in L.A. In short, you could eat nothing but tacos and leave happily. Sit down for barbacoa tacos at Gish Bac , run by barbacoa queen Maria Ramos; bite into crispy fish and shrimp tacos from Tacos Baja 's three outposts; or pull up a red plastic stool at El Ruso , known for its carne asada. Of course, California's largest city offers every type of cuisine—from Burmese and Indian at Bagan Burmese Kitchen and Pijja Palace in Silver Lake to Italian at the Michelin-starred Osteria Mozza and Thai-Japanese fusion Budonoki in Hollywood and East Hollywood.

Whether you're after impossibly fresh poke and sushi, Korean barbecue, or oceanfront brunch, you'll find it in the Hawaiian capital. You'll be spoiled for choice when it comes to poke: Try the beloved Maguro Brothers , Kahiau , or Kyung's Seafood , which also has delicious kimchi pancakes. Inaba is as popular for soba and dizzying tempura options as it is for sushi and has an expansive lunch menu that's very reasonably priced compared to top-notch but pricy options like Sushi Gyoshin . If you want a break from seafood, go for the lunch set at Korean barbecue joint Hangang or an oceanfront brunch at Hau Tree . For a refreshing post-beach treat, get a Hawaiian shave ice; you'll find shops and kiosks selling them all over Honolulu, but Aloha Ice Labs is particularly popular.

articles.title: Chess: 'I was beating adults at chess when I was eight'
articles.summary: Last week 13-year-old Ethan became the youngest Ulster Chess champion in history across all ages.
articles.body:
"When I was eight or nine I was beating adults at chess and they were raging when they lost, like 'I just lost to a little kid'."

Ethan first became interested in chess when he was six years old after he spotted someone else playing.

Now 13, he plays for Strand Chess Club in east Belfast and has represented Ireland through all his age groups.

Last week he became the youngest Ulster chess champion in history – not just in his age category but across all ages.

"I was really surprised because I've never won any of the big tournaments before, I've always got so close and I managed to win it in the end," Ethan told BBC News NI.

He said his opponents ranged from the ages of 30-65, all at least more than twice his age.

"That age range is the ages I've been playing against and I didn't get any losses. I got three wins and three draws."

Ethan said he enjoys the mental challenge of chess.

"I quite like the thinking part and the opening preparation.

"The game itself looks really interesting but there is so much more that goes into it before with preparation and tactics.

"I think I just had a natural ability from the start which I think was quite useful but I think starting at a young age helps quite a lot because it's easier to get it into your brain.

"I practice a lot and... I'm good at maths. I've got quite a good calculating ability. I think that's probably my main strength."

'If you're good enough you're old enough'

Neither of Ethan's parents are chess players.

However, his mum Eimear Savage said her son was fascinated with the chess board and pieces the moment he first saw them.

"It was a chance circumstance that Ethan saw someone play chess and thought it looked interesting and he decided he wanted to play and it went from there."

She said Ethan's success is all down to himself but his family support him every step of the way.

"I think Ethan just takes it in his stride and that's him. He enjoys playing chess and he enjoys taking part and when he wins it's a bonus.

"Ethan has been playing for a while now so people are used to playing against him but maybe when he was younger, I remember he wasn't quite tall enough to see over the table and he had to kneel up on the chair to get a good view of the pieces.

"That was always a bit of a spectacle but people know him now."

Ethan has played as part of the Irish team and has travelled to Paris where he played at the Eiffel Tower, as well as travelling to the Netherlands, Germany and Estonia for tournaments.

Ethan is certainly making a name for himself and his success isn't any surprise to his fellow members at Strand Chess Club.

Gareth Annesley said Ethan is a very tough opponent.

"You wouldn't think he's that young. You think you've got him and he just keeps on playing these moves and it's hard to beat him. He's very resourceful and he's very mature for his age.

"Even though he's only 13 he's been around for several years, so he has more or less beaten most of the top players in Ulster, so it wasn't a complete shock.

"If you're good enough, you're old enough in chess really."

"I'm going to keep this up for the rest of my life.

"My next goal is probably to be Irish champion and then grand master probably. That's the main goal."

articles.title: Saúde mental dos homens: Dados alertam para casos no Setembro Amarelo | G1
articles.standfirst: Psicólogos avaliam que valores culturais potencializam o número de mortes por suicídio entre população do sexo masculino.
articles.summary: Especialistas em Sorocaba analisam como barreiras culturais afetam a saúde mental dos homens e a prevenção ao suicídio durante o Setembro Amarelo.
articles.body:
O olhar para os números sobre saúde mental no Brasil se direciona especialmente a uma parte da população: os homens. Eles figuram entre as principais vítimas do sofrimento psíquico que leva à morte.

De acordo com o Atlas da Violência, levantamento feito pelo Fórum Brasileiro de Segurança Pública, no estado de São Paulo, aproximadamente 78,8% dos casos de suicídio ocorrem com eles. Em Sorocaba (SP), a rede pública de saúde registrou mais de 13 mil atendimentos psicológicos de janeiro a agosto de 2026. Somado aos atendimentos psiquiátricos, esse número representa um aumento de 5% na rede municipal em comparação ao mesmo período no ano anterior.

Uma oportunidade de enfrentamento desta realidade está no ato de desmistificar a busca pelo tratamento profissional e conscientizar as pessoas sobre as ferramentas de cuidado e preservação da saúde mental. É por esta razão que campanhas como a do Setembro Amarelo ganham espaço em diferentes ambientes da sociedade.

Pesquisa indica que homens são as principais vítimas de suicídio — Foto: Freepik

Dandriê Crestani é psicólogo e atua diariamente com atendimento clínico a pessoas que procuram ajuda profissional. Ele explica que, para muitos homens, o primeiro passo de reconhecer os sintomas do mal-estar mental é a maior dificuldade.

O isolamento social, a mudança de humor e o silêncio diante destas aflições são fatores que potencializam o sofrimento de quem precisa, na verdade, de ajuda especializada.

“Quando a gente fala que 80% das vítimas são do sexo masculino, a gente tá obviamente diante de uma questão que também envolve a maneira como os homens são socialmente ensinados a lidar com o sofrimento. O fracasso, a perda, as vulnerabilidades... Isso é uma questão cultural e coletiva, porque ao longo da vida muitos homens aprendem que precisam ser fortes, independentes, provedores e capazes de resolver seus próprios problemas custe o que custar ”, comenta.

O psicólogo alerta: "A pessoa pode estar passando, por exemplo, por um problema financeiro muito grave, alguma perda considerável dentro da família ou um fracasso profissional. E aí, em vez de procurar ajuda, ela vai tentar suportar isso tudo sozinha. É assim que temos o começo e a morada de todo o sofrimento".

Dandriê Crestani atua como psicólogo clínico e organizacional há 13 anos — Foto: Dandriê Crestani / Arquivo pessoal

O resultado é a sequência de adoecimento psíquico. Alterações no sono, abuso de substâncias, comportamentos impulsivos e compulsivos, são mais alguns dos sintomas.

Rodrigo Pierobon, psicólogo e coordenador do curso de Psicologia na Faculdade Anhanguera, indica que enxerga uma mudança positiva neste comportamento da comunidade mais jovem.

“Nós estamos passando por uma transformação na sociedade, que ainda levará alguns bons anos, mas que isso tá sendo desmistificado. Isso se dá muito por dois pontos principais de transformação. Primeiro nós tivemos uma mudança muito grande na legislação, obrigando as empresas a tratarem do assunto de saúde mental dentro dos postos de trabalho. E também hoje, desde muito pequeno, as crianças já ouvem falar sobre a saúde mental, sobre a importância de falar sobre sentimentos”, pontua.

Jean Camargo, hoje com 22 anos, é exemplo desta mudança. O jovem conta que seu primeiro contato com terapia foi aos nove anos. "Na minha casa nunca foi tabu. Eu passei por acompanhamento em um período da infância e depois, mais velho, quis voltar por conta própria, justamente porque isso sempre foi valorizado".

Além do apoio dentro de casa, Jean também cita que em seus grupos de amigos, percebe uma facilidade em discutir saúde mental e reconhecer a escuta profissional.

"Na época da escola, de fato não era um assunto recorrente, mas em toda oportunidade que tinha, eu comentava da minha experiência. Já mais tarde, na faculdade, pelo menos três amigos também faziam terapia, e a gente conversava sobre", diz.

Jean Camargo buscou ajuda profissional em diferentes períodos da vida — Foto: Jean Camargo / Arquivo pessoal

Diferente de Jean, Sergio Pena, de 26 anos, vem de uma experiência que não foge a regra. Na sua casa, o exemplo foi um cenário mais comum da realidade brasileira: "O meu pai também não fala muito sobre as coisas que ele pensa ou sobre como ele se sente no geral. E eu sempre fui igual, mais quieto. Odiava falar como eu me sentia, mas eu tenho treinado muito isso. É o que eu estou trabalhando em terapia", relata.

Aos 18 anos, o jovem buscou romper com essa referência do silêncio. Com a dificuldade de verbalizar e o isolamento social, Sergio percebeu que o sofrimento estava afetando também a sua saúde física.

"Eu fui descobrir que desenvolvi uma gastrite nervosa. Tratei a ansiedade por uns quatro anos em terapia e, desde então eu sou, como bem dizer, outra pessoa, tipo de um jeito melhor. Pelo menos nunca mais fiquei sem comer ou sem dormir por conta disso", relembra.

Nessa atitude de buscar ajuda profissional e perceber os resultados, Sergio influenciou também o bem-estar de outras pessoas ao seu redor. "Eu fui meio que o precursor de fazer terapia na minha família. Hoje pelo menos minha mãe e minha irmã também fazem acompanhamento", conta.

Sergio procurou ajuda psicológica após perceber níveis de ansiedade fora do comum — Foto: Sérgio Pena / Arquivo pessoal

Apesar do fortalecimento de assuntos de saúde mental no público jovem, o professor Rodrigo faz questão de ressaltar que o adoecimento se apresenta também de forma "atualizada", diante dos contextos contemporâneos.

"O isolamento social é um sintoma, certo. E aí hoje temos os casos de quando a gente nota adolescentes e jovens envolvidos com jogos eletrônicos, que ficam muitas horas isoladas socialmente. A compulsão e o vício, um exemplo que temos visto muito também nos mais velhos, é a questão dos jogos de azar, o 'tigrinho', que também tem acometido uma grande parcela da população", diz.

Rodrigo Pierobon é mestre em psicologia organizacional e é coordenador do curso de graduação em psicologia da Faculdade Anhanguera, em Sorocaba — Foto: Rodrigo Pierobon / Arquivo pessoal

Ainda nesta análise da atualidade, Rodrigo complementa sobre outro cenário que atrai, principalmente, os homens. Uma vez que um sintoma do sofrimento patológico é o isolamento social, a oferta de acolhimento em grupos que naturalizam certos comportamentos da "cultura masculina" reforçam o adoecimento da população.

"Todo grupo ele é importante em determinado grau, porém quando você tá em um grupo que reforça essas características de autossuficiência, de que você não precisa pedir ajuda, de que o homem ele tem que dar conta de tudo, que ele tem que sofrer calado e que ele tem que superar — que é o que a comunidade Red Pill proporciona — Esse tipo de discurso ele não ajuda. Ele atrapalha, inclusive", finaliza.

💡O movimento Red Pill ganhou notoriedade na internet depois que homens começaram a abordar ideologias misóginas em seus discursos. A comunidade surgiu a partir de um conceito fictício do filme Matrix, de 1999, em que a pílula vermelha seria a escolha para "despertar" e ganhar "consciência" da realidade do mundo.

Em Sorocaba, é possível encontrar atendimento profissional gratuito na rede pública de saúde e também em clínicas-escola por valores acessíveis. Veja abaixo os endereços.

articles.title: Bugio-ruivo se equilibra em fios e chama atenção em SP; VÍDEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Animal foi registrado na Serra do Guaraú, em Peruíbe. Fundação Florestal diz que presença da espécie é natural na região e alerta para os riscos da rede elétrica.
articles.summary: Animal foi registrado na Serra do Guaraú, em Peruíbe. Fundação Florestal diz que presença da espécie é natural na região e alerta para os riscos da rede elétrica.
articles.body:
Um bugio-ruivo foi visto caminhando sobre fios de energia elétrica na Serra do Guaraú, em Peruíbe , no litoral de São Paulo. Imagens que circulam nas redes sociais mostram pessoas que passavam pela região observando e gravando o animal enquanto ele se deslocava pela fiação.

“Em uma estradinha aqui do Guaraú, Peruíbe, olha o que a gente viu aqui [...] Que show, hein!”, disse a pessoa que gravou o vídeo. “Não se encontra um desse em qualquer esquina”, acrescentou.

A Neoenergia Elektro, responsável pelo fornecimento de energia na região, informou que as redes de baixa e média tensão possuem revestimento de proteção que ajuda a reduzir o risco de choques elétricos em animais silvestres.

Bugio-ruivo foi registrado andando sobre fios em Peruíbe (SP). — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Em nota, a Fundação Florestal explicou que a presença de bugios-ruivos (Alouatta guariba) na Serra do Guaraú faz parte da distribuição natural da espécie na Mata Atlântica do litoral sul paulista.

Segundo a fundação, o comportamento de se deslocar por fios elétricos não é incomum, embora a rede de energia possa representar risco aos animais.

A Fundação Florestal informou ainda que não houve registro de incidente envolvendo o bugio visto nas imagens e orientou moradores e visitantes a não interferirem no comportamento da fauna silvestre.

Segundo o biólogo Eric Comin, o bugio-ruivo é um animal arborícola, que vive principalmente nas copas das árvores e raramente desce ao solo. A alimentação é composta principalmente por folhas, frutos, brotos e sementes.

Em locais onde há interrupções na vegetação, explicou o biólogo, os animais podem utilizar estruturas como postes, cercas e fios elétricos para se deslocar.

De acordo com Comin, os machos adultos apresentam pelagem ruiva ou avermelhada, enquanto fêmeas e filhotes têm coloração castanho-escura. O bugio também é conhecido pela vocalização intensa, que pode ser ouvida a quilômetros de distância.

A espécie sofre com a perda e a fragmentação do habitat, além de outros riscos associados à presença humana. Os bugios também são bastante suscetíveis à febre amarela e, segundo Comin, funcionam como importantes sentinelas da circulação do vírus nas áreas de mata.

articles.summary: Vítima de tentativa de feminicídio em maio deste ano, no Ceará, a jovem Ana Clara fala ao g1 sobre autoestima, recuperação do movimento dos membros e planos para o futuro.
articles.body:
“Uma nova fase, uma nova vida”. É assim que Ana Clara Antero de Oliveira , de 21 anos, que teve uma mão decepada e a outra parcialmente mutilada em uma tentativa de feminicídio no Ceará, define a nova rotina após quatro meses da tragédia. A jovem ficou quase um mês internada no Instituto Doutor José Frota (IJF), na capital, onde passou pelo reimplante das duas mãos.

O crime ocorreu em Quixeramobim , no interior do Ceará, a cerca de 200 quilômetros de Fortaleza , no dia 1º de maio. Os suspeitos do crime, o ex-namorado de Ana Clara, Ronivaldo Rocha dos Santos, e o irmão dele, Evangelista Rocha dos Santos, foram presos e se tornaram réus por tentativa de feminicídio.

Após o trauma, Ana mantém a esperança de recuperar completamente os movimentos dos membros e traça dois novos objetivos: cursar faculdade de Direito para ajudar outras mulheres vítimas de violência e se tornar uma ativista da causa.

Em nova entrevista ao g1 , ela detalhou como tem sido a rotina, entre tratamento médico, palestras e recuperação da autoestima.

Ana Clara, vítima de tentativa de feminicídio, reflete sobre o caso. — Foto: Imagens cedidas por Bruno Sousa (@brunosousafotografia).

Ana Clara teve avanços ao longo de quase quatro meses de tratamento e fisioterapia nas mãos . Ela já consegue segurar objetos leves, se alimentar sozinha na maior parte do tempo e voltou a usar o celular, tarefa importante para se comunicar com familiares e amigos.

A jovem revelou ao g1 que passará por um novo procedimento para recuperar o movimento de "pinça", essencial para a coordenação motora.

“A recuperação das mãos também está indo muito bem. Vou passar agora por uma nova cirurgia para soltar os tendões, e aí os movimentos vão ficar bem melhores. É um processo lento. Eu ainda não consigo vestir uma roupa nem tomar banho sozinha, mas na fisioterapia a gente vê bastante avanço”, disse.

Ana Clara Antero, vítima de tentativa de feminicídio, fala sobre processo de recuperação após reimplante das mãos — Foto: Ismael Soares/SVM

A cearense está morando em Fortaleza com a família para facilitar as idas ao hospital e o tratamento físico. A ideia é continuar na capital, onde pretende estudar e se dedicar ao combate à violência contra a mulher.

No último mês, Ana Clara passou por cerca de 15 cidades participando de eventos e palestras. Mesmo relembrando momentos de dor, ela afirma que falar sobre o caso ajuda a superar a tragédia e a recuperar a autoestima.

“No mês de agosto quase todo, eu andei em várias cidades fazendo palestras, falando um pouco da minha história para as pessoas. E a gente vê o absurdo do tanto de gente que passa ou passou pela mesma situação e que, infelizmente, ainda não consegue sair. A violência contra a mulher, a cada dia que passa, está crescendo mais”, afirmou.

Nas palestras, Ana Clara usa o microfone para compartilhar a própria história, mas também para alertar o público sobre a importância de proteger as mulheres e denunciar possíveis agressores.

Ela também reconhece hoje que o antigo relacionamento se encaixa no chamado ciclo da violência , conceito formulado pela psicóloga norte-americana Lenore Walker.

“Isso que eu faço hoje, ser uma pessoa ativista, é uma responsabilidade muito grande. Eu costumo alertar essas mulheres sobre como elas podem perceber os sinais. A agressão não acontece só no extremo, existe um ciclo. Os sinais são, por exemplo, ele dizer: ‘não gosto dessa roupa’, ‘não quero que você vá à casa da sua família’, ‘quero que você pare de estudar’. Eu passei por isso e achava que era amor, mas a gente precisa entender que isso não é amor, não é cuidado”, afirmou.

Ana Clara fala ao g1 sobre autoestima e beleza. — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Grata por estar viva, Ana Clara se diz mais confiante e vê uma oportunidade de recomeçar. Ela ganhou uma bolsa de estudos para o curso de Direito e pretende atuar como advogada voluntária na defesa de mulheres que passaram por situações semelhantes.

Em meio a tantas demandas, ela também encontra tempo para cuidar do emocional por meio da espiritualidade e da fé. Questionada sobre como mantém a serenidade mesmo após o trauma, Ana Clara afirma que sua força vem de Deus, mas não descarta fazer terapia.

“Sei que vai chegar um momento em que eu vou precisar de terapia, mas, no momento, vejo que meu emocional está bem, eu sou forte. Todos os dias eu apago um pouco do que eu passei no dia 1º de maio ”, disse.

Outro aspecto do processo de fortalecimento é o cuidado com a aparência. Vaidosa, Ana Clara não abre mão de cuidar dos cabelos, da pele e de escolher looks confortáveis para ir à igreja ou às palestras. Ela diz que deixou a vaidade de lado por um tempo, mas considera importante resgatar esse cuidado nesta nova fase.

“No início, eu ficava um pouco para baixo. Só que, naquele momento, a autoestima não era o mais importante. O importante era a minha recuperação. Mas, hoje, eu me sinto bem, minha autoestima está alta. Estou tendo acompanhamento com dentista. A gente precisa mudar para que a autoestima se encaixe na minha nova fase”, contou.

Aos 21 anos, ela entende que o crime sofrido não define quem ela é. Mesmo após o trauma, afirma estar vivendo “a melhor fase da vida” , ao lado da família e dos novos amigos que conheceu depois da repercussão do caso.

“Posso dizer que estou vivendo a melhor fase da minha vida, infelizmente nessa situação, mas não tenho nada a reclamar, e sim só agradecer a Deus por estar viva e poder ter a chance de recomeçar tudo do zero. Sou uma jovem que sonha, apesar do trauma, em construir uma família, que pensa em conhecer outra pessoa. Mas minha pressa é focar nos estudos e trabalhar por essas mulheres que não têm condições de pagar um advogado ”, concluiu.

Quatro meses após o crime, Ana Clara recupera autoestima e planeja estudar. — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

articles.title: Violência doméstica: 8 em 10 beneficiárias têm filhos | G1
articles.standfirst: Programa municipal concedeu 337 benefícios desde 2023; 297 mulheres atendidas são mães e somam 718 filhos ou dependentes.
articles.summary: Programa municipal concedeu 337 benefícios desde 2023; 297 mulheres atendidas são mães e somam 718 filhos ou dependentes.
articles.body:
Violência contra a mulher — Foto: © Paulo H. Carvalho/Agência Brasília

A Prefeitura de Campinas (SP) concedeu 337 benefícios de auxílio-moradia para vítimas de violência doméstica desde a criação do programa, em 2023, até agosto de 2026.

De acordo com a Secretaria Municipal de Assistência Social, do total de mulheres atendidas no período, 88,1% tinham ao menos um filho , sendo que a maioria era menor de 6 anos.

Os dados revelam que a oferta do benefício tem crescido nos últimos anos. O número de auxílios pagos de janeiro a agosto de 2026 superou os 12 meses do ano passado.

🏡 O auxílio-moradia é um benefício temporário emergencial concedido às vítimas que precisam deixar o lar por motivo de violência doméstica. As mulheres recebem R$ 951 por mês , por até seis meses consecutivos, e o valor deve ser usado exclusivamente para pagar aluguel.

Das mulheres que receberam o auxílio desde a criação do programa, 297 são mães e totalizam 718 filhos/dependentes registrados – dos quais 83% são menores de 18 anos.

O levantamento também indica que a maior parcela do benefício se concentra entre mulheres de 30 a 39 anos (34,4%). A faixa de 20 a 49 anos representa 88,1% do total de atendidas.

No recorte por cor, 60,2% das 337 beneficiadas ao longo do período são negras (pretas e pardas).

Como acessar o auxílio-moradia em Campinas

O benefício é exclusivo para mulheres em situação de violência acompanhadas pelos Centros de Referência Especializados de Assistência Social (Creas) e o Abrigo Sara-M.

ser encaminhada pela rede socioassistencial.

São necessários também documento de identidade com foto e CPF, além de comprovante de endereço.

A Secretaria de Desenvolvimento Social do Estado de São Paulo (SEDS) também disponibiliza auxílio-aluguel às vítimas de violência doméstica. O programa oferece uma ajuda de custo mensal de R$ 500 por seis meses, com possibilidade de renovação por igual período.

Na região de Campinas, 19 municípios aderiram ao programa . Desde a criação do programa, em fevereiro de 2025, até agosto de 2026, foram concedidos 448 benefícios na região, de acordo com informações enviadas pela pasta.

"Romper o ciclo da violência doméstica exige mais do que coragem, é necessário apoio real e condições concretas para um recomeço seguro. O auxílio-aluguel, além de um importante suporte financeiro, é uma ferramenta de autonomia e dignidade para que essas mulheres possam reescrever suas histórias longe do medo", afirma a secretária de Desenvolvimento Social, Andrezza Rosalém.

Auxílio-aluguel para vítimas da violência na região de Campinas

Para solicitar o benefício, é necessário apresentar:

comprovante de residência atualizado no Estado de São Paulo;

cópia da medida protetiva de urgência expedida pelo Poder Judiciário (Lei Maria da Penha);

comprovantes de renda que demonstrem que a renda familiar, até a separação, era de até dois salários mínimos;

comprovação de vulnerabilidade social (como o número do CadÚnico atualizado ou relatório psicossocial).

O cadastramento é feito pela rede municipal de assistência social nos municípios participantes. Após análise e aprovação, o valor é disponibilizado por meio de Poupança Social no Banco do Brasil, diretamente às beneficiárias.

Além do suporte financeiro, o programa articula outras políticas públicas municipais, ampliando o acesso a serviços de proteção social, orientação e acompanhamento às mulheres atendidas em todo o estado. Veja onde buscar atendimento:

Assistência Social: CRAS, CREAS e Centros de Referência de Atendimento à Mulher;

Saúde: Unidade Básica de Saúde (UBS), pronto-socorro e hospitais;

Segurança Pública: Delegacia de Defesa da Mulher (DDM), distrito policial, batalhão da Polícia Militar e Corpo de Bombeiros;

Sistema de Justiça: Ministério Público, Defensoria Pública e Ordem dos Advogados do Brasil;

Canais de orientação e denúncia: Ligue 180 (Central de Atendimento à Mulher) e 190, para emergências.

articles.title: SC define rotas, horários e preços de voos regionais; veja destinos | G1
articles.standfirst: Serviço vai começar em 3 de novembro e conectar 10 cidades catarinenses por via aérea. Passagens vão custar entre R$ 315 e R$ 815.
articles.summary: Serviço vai começar em 3 de novembro e conectar 10 cidades catarinenses por via aérea.
articles.body:
Santa Catarina definiu as rotas, horários e preços do projeto de voos regionais , que vai conectar 10 cidades do estado em uma malha aérea. Tudo começa a valer a partir de 3 de novembro .

A companhia aérea Azul vai operar os voos, com ligações entre os aeroportos regionais e Florianópolis . As passagens vão custar entre R$ 315 e R$ 815 e começam a ser vendidas em 28 de setembro.

🧳O valor das passagens inclui serviço de bordo e o despacho gratuito de bagagem de mão e uma mala até 23 quilos .

Com a medida, uma viagem de Florianópolis a Joinville que levaria, em média, pouco mais de 2 horas de carro, pode levar 55 minutos de avião. Da capital até Joaçaba , a média é de seis horas de automóvel. Já o voo leva 1h30.

Os cálculos e velocidades dos voos foram confirmados pela companhia aérea, mas podem ser mais rápidos ou lentos dependendo das condições climáticas, conforme a Secretaria de Portos, Aeroportos e Ferrovias de Santa Catarina (veja estimativas abaixo).

articles.title: União estável é reconhecida após homem alegar 'apenas amizade' em SC | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão considerou fotos, mensagens, documentos e registros financeiros apresentados no processo. Sentença reconheceu convivência entre outubro de 2007 e janeiro de 2017.
articles.summary: A Justiça de Santa Catarina reconheceu a união estável homoafetiva e determinou a partilha de bens após analisar provas de convivência por uma década.
articles.body:
A Justiça de Santa Catarina reconheceu a união estável homoafetiva entre dois homens que viveram juntos por quase 10 anos, mesmo após um deles alegar que havia apenas "amizade" entre eles.

A decisão foi divulgada na última terça-feira (8) pela 1ª Vara da comarca de Penha , no Litoral Norte. Como o processo tramita em segredo, os nomes dos envolvidos não foram divulgados.

De acordo com o TJSC, o casal compartilhou residência, rotina doméstica, viagens e projetos de vida de outubro de 2007 a janeiro de 2017.

Eles também trabalharam juntos em negócios, incluindo a construção e a administração de um empreendimento turístico, além da compra e reforma de imóveis.

A decisão também declarou o fim do relacionamento e determinou a partilha dos bens adquiridos durante a convivência, após a análise de documentos, fotos e registros financeiros.

Homem alegou que relação era 'apenas de amizade'

Um dos homens contestou a união. Ele alegou que havia apenas amizade e cooperação profissional entre eles, e sustentou que comprou os bens em discussão exclusivamente com recursos próprios.

Apesar disso, a juíza considerou provada a convivência contínua e duradoura.

Ela analisou fotos dos dois em eventos familiares e mensagens que mostravam planos em comum.

A magistrada também usou como provas comprovantes de residência , notas fiscais , registros imobiliários e uma procuração pública de 2012 , com poderes recíprocos, que reforçaram a existência do núcleo familiar.

A decisão destacou que o fato de alguns familiares não saberem do relacionamento não impede o reconhecimento da união estável diante das outras provas apresentadas.

bandeira lgbt lgbtqia+ arco-iris — Foto: JL Rosa/SVM

Justiça determinou divisão igualitária de bens

Com a decisão, a Justiça determinou a divisão igualitária dos bens adquiridos durante a união . A partilha inclui:

Imóveis comprados antes do relacionamento ficaram fora da divisão. No entanto, as melhorias feitas em um deles, durante a convivência, deverão ser avaliadas em uma etapa posterior do processo.

A juíza negou os pedidos de condenação por litigância de má-fé feitos por ambas as partes, por entender que as versões conflitantes não demonstraram intenção deliberada de enganar a Justiça.

articles.title: Kate Mosse's new book is a 'love letter' to Sussex in the autumn
articles.summary: Author Kate Mosse says Sussex in autumn is "like nowhere else" as her latest book is published.
articles.body:
Best-selling author Kate Mosse has said Sussex in autumn is "like nowhere else" as she marks the publication of her latest book exploring the season.

The Chichester-based writer said Autumn: The Story of a Season draws inspiration from Sussex landscapes including Fishbourne marshes, Chanctonbury Ring and Devil's Dyke, as well as traditions such as the Lewes bonfire celebrations.

"It's a book about memory, belonging. It's a book about what it means to come from somewhere," she said.

"It's my love letter to Sussex. It's very much about the season.

"It's part of a series. Michael Morpurgo wrote Spring, Val McDermid wrote Winter, Bernardine Evaristo, the Booker Prize winner, is writing Summer.

"So autumn is my favourite season, and Sussex in the autumn, there is nowhere like it."

Her latest book came out on Thursday, but Mosse is already working on her next novel, Borderlands, which is due to be published next year.

"It's set partly in Bosham and Hastings in 1064 and 1066 and the modern day, and then a lot of it is set in the mysterious, very spooky tidal island of the Mont Saint-Michel in Normandy," she said.

"It's inspired by the Sussex history of the Norman conquest and all of this kind of thing, but also my own family history."

The writer said she had a family tree dating back to 1066 when a Mosse had served in the army of William the Conqueror.

"When he survived the Battle of Hastings, he decided Sussex was a very nice place to live. And so he stayed."

Mosse said she had always wanted to write about her own family history.

Her book is due to be published following the exhibition of the Bayeux Tapestry in London, and before an exhibition at the British Library next autumn about the Normans, ahead of the 1,000th anniversary of the birth of William the Conqueror in 2027, she said.

The author described her next project as "a big old novel", adding that she had already been working on it for a couple of years.

articles.title: West Country accent 'would not have worked for Oasis', says Noel
articles.summary: The comments were made in the band's new documentary 'Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger'.
articles.body:
Oasis would not have worked if the band had "a West Country accent", Noel Gallagher has said.

He made the claim in a new documentary, 'Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger', which tells the story of the band's reunion and comeback tour after 15 years apart.

Talking about the importance of the band's Manchester roots, Gallagher said: "Imagine if I had a West Country accent saying 'we are going to be the biggest band in the world'. It's not gonna work."

Despite his comment, Oasis does reportedly have a West Country connection. A long-held rumour suggests their name was inspired by Swindon's Oasis Leisure Centre , which hosted a gig which Gallagher worked on as a guitar technician.

The documentary, which is currently in cinemas, was produced by Gloucestershire-based Steven Knight who created Peaky Blinders and co-created Who Wants to be a Millionaire.

Despite this, Bristol and the wider West Country has produced a host of high-profile media figures like Simon Pegg, Stephen Merchant and Maisie Williams, as well as musicians such as Massive Attack, Idles and two thirds of Bananarama.

But arguably none have embraced their West Country accent as fervently as the Wurzels, who topped the charts in 1976 with Somerset anthem, 'The Combine Harvester' .

"I think if we'd done [our music] in a Mancuinian accent it wouldn't have worked for us!" said Wurzels front man, Pete Budd.

"We're proud of our West Country accent and I'm sure that Noel Gallagher is proud of his Mancunian accent."

"Noel Gallagher is probably right in what he says - Oasis are Oasis and are one of the biggest bands in the world," he added.

"He knows what he's talking about but I would think it's a little bit tongue in cheek as well."

Despite staunchly defending the West Country accent, Budd said that what really matters for bands is the music they release.

"If people like a particular song, I don't think its the accent, it's the music and the way you do it," he said.

articles.title: Meet  Eknath Vasant Chitnis: The man who helped build ISRO, recognized the potential of a young APJ Abdul Kalam and brought satellite TV to Indian villages
articles.summary: India's space programme has produced some of the country's best-known scientists, but not every name associated with its early years is equally famili.
articles.body: India's space programme has produced some of the country's best-known scientists, but not every name associated with its early years is equally familiar. Professor Eknath Vasant Chitnis was one of those lesser-known figures whose work helped shape the foundations of Indian space research. Chitnis was a founding pioneer of India's space programme and a close associate of Dr Vikram Sarabhai, widely regarded as the father of India's space programme. Chitnis died at the age of 100 on October 22, 2025. His life offers a look at the scientists who helped build India's space programme before it became the global name it is today.Losing his parents at a young ageEknath Vasant Chitnis was born on July 25, 1925, in Kolhapur, Maharashtra. He lost both his parents at a young age and was raised by his grandmother. He went on to study physics in Pune. His first professional experience was with All India Radio, but his interest in science soon took him to the Physical Research Laboratory (PRL) in Ahmedabad.PRL had been founded by Vikram Sarabhai, who was working to establish a scientific base for India's future space research. It was at PRL that Chitnis became involved in the early work that would eventually connect him with the country's space programme.The scientist who worked with Vikram SarabhaiAt PRL, Chitnis contributed to research in space physics. He built Cerenkov Counters, instruments used to study cosmic rays. He later collaborated with the research group of Professor Bruno Rossi at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). The work helped establish his scientific credentials before he returned to India in the early 1960s.His association with Sarabhai became important during the early years of India's space programme. Chitnis was involved in shaping Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR), which was established in 1962 and later developed into ISRO. The early programme was not simply about sending rockets into space. Sarabhai and his colleagues saw space technology as a way to address practical needs in a developing country, including communications, education and scientific research. Chitnis became part of that effort.How he helped select Thumba for India's first rocket launchesOne of Chitnis's important contributions came during the search for a suitable location for India's first rocket launch site. His fieldwork and scientific assessment helped lead to the selection of Thumba in Kerala. The location was important because of its proximity to the Earth's magnetic equator, making it suitable for atmospheric studies and early space research.Chitnis was instrumental in the selection of Thumba as the site for India's first rocket launches. The first sounding rocket was launched from Thumba on November 21, 1963. The launch marked an early milestone in India's space journey. Chitnis later helped identify Sriharikota in Andhra Pradesh as a launch site, which would eventually become India's principal spaceport.The man who recognised APJ Abdul Kalam's potentialOne of the most interesting details in Chitnis's career is his connection with Dr APJ Abdul Kalam. Before Kalam became the scientist who led India's missile development and later served as the country's President, he was a young aerospace engineer looking for opportunities in India's developing space programme.According to a TOI report, Chitnis was credited with recruiting Kalam into ISRO after reviewing his resume and recognising his potential. That decision brought together two important figures in India's scientific history. Kalam would go on to become one of the country's most celebrated scientists, while Chitnis continued to work in the development of space applications. The recruitment story is one of the reasons Chitnis's name has attracted renewed attention after his death.How he helped bring satellite television to Indian villagesChitnis's work was not limited to rockets and launch sites. He also played a role in the effort to use space technology for everyday public needs. As member secretary of INCOSPAR and later as Director of ISRO's Space Applications Centre, he worked on applications of satellite technology. One of the most significant projects associated with his career was the Satellite Instructional Television Experiment, or SITE.The experiment that took television to rural IndiaThe Satellite Instructional Television Experiment was conducted in 1975–76 using NASA's ATS-6 satellite. The experiment beamed educational programmes to 2,400 remote villages across India. The project demonstrated how satellites could be used to deliver information and educational content to communities that did not have easy access to conventional communication systems. For India, this was an important step towards the wider use of satellite communications. The experiment also became a forerunner to the INSAT programme, which later played a major role in the country's telecommunications and broadcasting development.When he won Padma Bhushan in 1985Chitnis was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1985 for his contributions to science. He also served as chairman of the Press Trust of India and continued his association with academic life. He lectured for decades at Savitribai Phule Pune University. His career therefore extended beyond ISRO and space research. He was involved in science, education and public communication.A scientist whose work shaped India's space journeyThe story of Indian space research is often told through the achievements of Vikram Sarabhai, Satish Dhawan, APJ Abdul Kalam and later generations of scientists. Chitnis belonged to the generation that helped build the institutions and systems on which those achievements depended. He died in 2025, but the projects he helped develop remain part of the history of India's space programme.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: BRICS nations urge smooth flow of global trade, supply chains, energy
articles.summary: Joint declaration at BRICS urges need to work together to maintain smooth flow of global trade, supply chains and energy
articles.body:
The BRICS group ⁠of nations has unanimously ⁠adopted a joint declaration, stressing the need to work together to maintain smooth flow of global trade, supply chains and energy.

India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who is hosting the two-day meeting in New Delhi, made the announcement on Saturday following the launch of the summit.

The presidency has fallen to New Delhi at a difficult moment, with wars in the Middle East and Ukraine disrupting energy and shipping, tariffs pressing on members, and the members at odds over how to answer either challenge.

Expansion of non-Western cross-border payment channels and cooperation on artificial intelligence are also key items on the agenda.

The annual BRICS summit opened in New Delhi, with China’s President Xi Jinping, Russia’s President Vladimir Putin and Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian among those attending.

President Xi arrived in the Indian capital on Saturday morning, his first visit to the country in seven years as the two Asian giants seek to thaw relations.

He said the fighting in the Middle East does not serve the world’s interests, reports Chinese state media.

“As the situation in the Middle East and the Gulf region continues to evolve, the war there has caused serious losses to people across the region,” Xinhua quoted Xi as saying.

It “does not serve the common interests of the international community”, Xi said.

On Friday, Modi held talks with Putin – agreeing to deepen ties – and with Pezeshkian, raising freedom of navigation and the safety of ship crews.

Egypt’s Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, Ethiopia’s Abiy Ahmed and Indonesia’s Prabowo Subianto are also in attendance. The UAE has sent the crown prince of Abu Dhabi as its representative. Founding member Brazil sent Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira to stand in for President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.

The heads of the World Health Organization, the World Trade Organization (WTO), and United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres are also present in India for the summit.

Iran and the United Arab Emirates, both members, are on opposing sides of the war waged on Iran by the United States and Israel.

Last year’s summit saw the bloc issue a joint declaration condemning the 12-day US-Israeli bombing campaign against Iran’s leadership and nuclear programme. But a meeting of BRICS foreign ministers in May this year ended without a joint statement on the conflict.

The bloc’s finance ministers and central bank governors have objected to tariffs and non-tariff measures they say distort trade and are inconsistent with WTO rules.

The US has levied tariffs on several members of the bloc under different pretexts, often conditioning their removal on policy changes by the target country. President Donald Trump has described the bloc as “anti-American” and threatened to impose punitive tariffs on countries that align with it.

“As the host, New Delhi has a delicate balancing act,” says Al Jazeera’s Um-e-Kulsoom Shariff, reporting from New Delhi.

“It has pressing issues to address: Trade, finance, technology, energy security, resilient supply chains and climate change. But as the alliance marks its 20th anniversary, the major test is whether its newly expanded membership can further empower the Global South.”

articles.title: Trump may be BRICS’s best recruitment agent
articles.summary: The US president wants to weaken BRICS, but he may end up doing the opposite.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump has made no secret of his hostility towards BRICS.

Last year, he threatened an additional 10 percent tariff on any country aligning itself with what he called the bloc’s “anti-American policies”. Since then, his administration has continued to wield tariffs aggressively against trading partners, including BRICS members such as Brazil, India and China.

The message appears straightforward: Countries that challenge US economic power should expect to pay a price.

But coercion has consequences. And as BRICS leaders meet in New Delhi today, Trump may be strengthening the very incentives that made the bloc attractive in the first place. The more Washington demonstrates its willingness to use access to its markets, its financial system and the dollar as instruments of political leverage, the more reason other countries have to reduce their exposure to them.

This does not mean BRICS is becoming an anti-US alliance. Far from it.

The bloc’s 11 members – Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates – have enormous political and economic differences. Together, they account for nearly half the world’s population and about 40 percent of global gross domestic product, but they do not share a common ideology, security policy or even geopolitical orientation.

Recent events have made those divisions impossible to ignore. Iran, Saudi Arabia and the UAE find themselves on opposite sides of a growing regional conflict. In May, Iranian and Emirati representatives clashed during a foreign ministers’ meeting in New Delhi. India and China have had a heated border dispute that led to deadly skirmishes in 2020-2021; only in the past two years have their relations gradually stabilised.

So Trump is not producing a united geopolitical front against Washington.

He may, however, be giving countries with otherwise divergent interests a common reason to cooperate economically: Protection against vulnerability to US power.

For countries outside the Western core, dependence on US-centred economic infrastructure carries risks.

The dollar’s centrality gives the US enormous structural advantages. International transactions pass through financial institutions subject to US jurisdiction; access to US markets can be restricted; sanctions can isolate governments and companies from parts of the global financial system.

BRICS’s efforts to diminish dependence on the US financial system do not mean the dollar is about to lose its position as a global reserve currency. This claim is often made around BRICS summits, usually accompanied by breathless predictions of a new BRICS currency. The evidence does not support it.

The dollar remains overwhelmingly dominant. According to the International Monetary Fund, it accounted for 57.1 percent of global foreign-exchange reserves in the first quarter of 2026. The Chinese renminbi accounted for just 2 percent. Indeed, the dollar’s share rose slightly during the quarter.

But replacing the dollar and reducing dependence on it are two very different things.

BRICS countries are already experimenting with the latter. South Africa has connected to China’s Cross-Border Interbank Payment System, allowing transactions with China to be settled directly in renminbi. Brazil and China are increasingly using their own currencies in bilateral trade, while India and the UAE have settled transactions in rupees and dirhams. China and Russia have shifted much of their bilateral trade into their national currencies.

BRICS itself is also moving cautiously towards greater financial connectivity.

Last year, its leaders called for continued work on a cross-border payments initiative and greater interoperability among members’ payment systems. In August, Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra confirmed that BRICS countries are discussing linking their fast-payment networks and potentially their central bank digital currencies. India itself is also encouraging greater use of the rupee in international trade.

The New Development Bank offers another example. Established by the original BRICS countries as an alternative source of development finance, it has made lending in members’ currencies an explicit strategic objective. Its current strategy targets 30 percent of financing in local currencies, partly to reduce borrowers’ exposure to foreign-exchange risks and costly currency swaps; the number could increase to 40-50 percent for the next cycle, 2027-2031.

None of this amounts to a rival global financial system. Much of it remains experimental, bilateral or limited in scale.

But that is precisely why the fixation on whether BRICS can “replace” the dollar misses what is happening. The more significant development is the gradual construction of options that allow governments and businesses to conduct a number of transactions without relying on the dollar and Western-dominated financial infrastructure.

Trump’s policies give this process additional urgency.

Consider Brazil. Washington imposed a new 25 percent tariff on a range of Brazilian products in July, affecting billions of dollars in exports, despite running a trade surplus with the country. The Trump administration has also scrutinised Brazil’s hugely successful Pix instant-payment system, which competes with established card-payment networks.

Sanctions demonstrate the same vulnerability more dramatically. Russia and Iran have been pushed towards alternative payment and trading arrangements precisely because their access to Western financial networks has been restricted. Washington is now considering further measures that could penalise countries heavily reliant on Russian energy, including China and India.

No BRICS member needs to sympathise with Moscow or Tehran to understand what this implies.

US financial power depends not simply on possessing the world’s largest economy or issuing its dominant currency. It also depends on other countries continuing to regard participation in a US-centred system as more advantageous than the alternatives.

The more frequently Washington turns that system into an instrument of coercion, the stronger the incentive to construct escape routes from it.

That said, most BRICS countries do not appear eager to exchange dependence on Washington for dependence on Beijing.

India maintains extensive relations with the US while buying Russian energy and pursuing closer economic cooperation within BRICS. Brazil has long sought greater autonomy without becoming a Chinese satellite. Saudi Arabia and the UAE remain deeply intertwined with Western economies while expanding their relationships with China.

Their objective is less likely to be replacing one hegemon with another than increasing their ability to manoeuvre between competing centres of power.

That distinction matters. A trade transaction settled in rupees, a loan denominated in renminbi or rand, or a payment made through a system that does not depend on the same Western intermediaries will not overthrow dollar dominance.

But multiply such arrangements across countries and over time, and they begin to reduce the costs of saying no to Washington.

This is why portraying BRICS simply as an anti-US threat risks becoming self-defeating. Punishing countries for seeking alternatives gives them another reason to develop those alternatives.

Trump wants to make challenging US power costly. Instead, he may be making dependence on US power costlier still.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

articles.title: In 2012, The Simpsons co-creator Sam Simon funded a Sea Shepherd ship; it later helped recover a reported 72 km of illegal nets during a 110-day poacher chase
articles.summary: Rest of World News: In 2012, The Simpsons co-creator Sam Simon financed a Sea Shepherd ship that removed 72 km of illegal nets and participated in a historic 110-day chase of poachers. Discover how this initiative impacted ocean conservation.
articles.body: This transition occurred near the end of 2012 when Sea Shepherd Conservation Society bought a former research ship owned by the Japanese government via a Delaware shell corporation called New Atlantis Ventures LLC. This corporation was listed on the documents as the owner of the ship while the involvement of Sea Shepherd was hidden, according to ABC News. After the purchase, a Japanese crew sailed the vessel to Australia and handed it over to Sea Shepherd. It was initially renamed New Atlantis, then publicly unveiled in Hobart, Tasmania, in December 2012 as the MY Sam Simon. It was renamed for Sam Simon, who co-created The Simpsons and had provided the money to buy the ship, according to his biography on the Television Academy's website.A television writer turned his royalties toward ocean conservationBefore joining Matt Groening and James L. Brooks in producing The Simpsons in 1989, Simon was already rich from writing scripts for shows such as Taxi and Cheers. Simon left the show after its fourth season but kept his executive producer credit, which earned him dollars in royalties over the years. In his later years, he channeled most of his money into animal-related charities like PETA, Save the Children and the Sam Simon Foundation. Through his connection with Paul Watson of Sea Shepherd, he decided to finance a boat for the group. The cost of MY Sam Simon was around $2 million, a price mentioned by media sources like The Guardian through Common Dreams and other coverage associated with Sea Shepherd.The ship's first mission targeted a whaling fleet's fuel supplyFirstly, the MY Sam Simon’s maiden voyage was utilized for targeting the Japanese whaling ships in the Southern Ocean under the mission called “Zero Tolerance,” as per Sea Shepherd’s own history of campaigns. They located the refueling vessel of the whaling fleet, Sun Laurel, and attempted to disrupt fuel transfers between this vessel and the harpoon vessels, as described by Sea Shepherd Australia. During the chase, there was a report of diesel leakage from the tanker, which they captured on video. As per reports in the media from ABC News about the 2012-2013 Antarctic season, the MY Sam Simon was working along with two more Sea Shepherd vessels, namely Steve Irwin and Bob Barker, following the Japanese whaling factory ship Nisshin Maru and trying to obstruct its refueling by February 2013.Operation Icefish sent two ships after six illegal trawlersIn December 2014, the two ships left New Zealand and Australia for a mission called “Icefish”, which was meant to serve a single purpose. The goal of the mission was to hunt down six fishing vessels labeled as the “Bandit 6” by Sea Shepherd, which were illegally fishing Patagonian toothfish using gillnets in the Southern Ocean, which was a practice outlawed by CCAMLR, the organization that manages the fisheries of Antarctica. On December 17, 2014, the Bob Barker stopped a ship belonging to the Bandit 6 fleet, the Thunder, as it tried to recover its gillnets from the Southern Ocean, as reported in the Operation Icefish reports of the Sea Shepherd Conservation Society. The Thunder released her gillnets and sped off.The Thunder chase ran 110 days across three oceansAccording to Sea Shepherd, the chase was the longest pursuit of an illegal fishing boat it had documented. Although the Bob Barker pursued the Thunder for 110 days through more than 10,000 nautical miles of the seas, covering the Southern Ocean and traversing two seas and three oceans, the Sam Simon refueled the first boat and gathered evidence during its pursuit, according to the report published by the United States Government Printing Office on Sea Shepherd. The hunt ended on April 6, 2015, when the ship ran aground within the exclusive economic zone of São Tomé and Príncipe in the Gulf of Guinea, as reported by Sea Shepherd in its incident report.Bob Barker, captain Peter Hammarstedt, said the Thunder showed clear signs of having been deliberately scuttled, its hatches tied open rather than sealed, which he suggested was meant to send any evidence of the illegal catch to the bottom of the ocean. Sea Shepherd's own account, corroborated by CNN and NBC News, says the Bob Barker and the ship Sam Simon together rescued all 40 of the Thunder's crew from life rafts before it went down, transferring them to the Sam Simon, whose crew then handed them over to the São Tomé coast guard. That October, the Supreme Court of São Tomé and Príncipe convicted the Thunder's captain and two of its engineers of forgery, pollution, and other charges tied to the sinking.Sam Simon's crew hauled up 72 kilometres of abandoned netWhile Bob Barker gave chase, Sam Simon stayed behind long enough to retrieve the illegal gillnet the Thunder had dropped in the Southern Ocean. Sea Shepherd said the net held toothfish worth an estimated $3 million. Sam Simon, who had been diagnosed with colorectal cancer in 2012, did not live to see the chase's end: he died on March 8, 2015, at his home in Los Angeles.Why gillnets and IUU fishing matterThe scale of the illegal toothfish fishing that produced groups like the Bandit 6 has been documented in fisheries research going back two decades. A 2000 paper in Marine Policy, "The illegal and unregulated fishery for toothfish in the Southern Ocean, and the CCAMLR catch documentation scheme" by David J. Agnew of Imperial College London, found that unregulated toothfish catches had grown so large that by the late 1990s they were running at about four times CCAMLR's regulated catch. The paper reveals that the fishing of Patagonian toothfish had started in the 1980s, and the illegal catches increased fourfold by 1997. It goes on to describe how the CCAMLR Catch Documentation Scheme of 1999 was developed in order to employ trade control to prevent IUU products from getting into the market. Nine years later, Agnew led a larger team, including researchers from Imperial College London and the University of British Columbia, on "Estimating the Worldwide Extent of Illegal Fishing," published in PLOS ONE in 2009, which put the annual value of illegal and unreported catches worldwide at $10 billion to $23.5 billion.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Lil Durk: Grammy-winning US rapper acquitted in murder-for-hire trial
articles.summary: The Chicago rapper was arrested in 2024 and accused of involvement in a shooting that killed the cousin of rival rapper Quando Rondo.
articles.body:
Grammy-winning rapper Lil Durk was acquitted on Friday of all charges in a federal murder-for-hire case accusing him of orchestrating the revenge killing of a man shot dead in a daytime ambush in Los Angeles four years ago.

The Chicago rapper was arrested in 2024 and accused of involvement in a shooting that killed the cousin of rival rapper Quando Rondo.

Defence lawyer Drew Findling said the recording artist, whose real name is Durk Devontay Banks, was "thankful" following the verdict.

Lil Durk has had seven albums in the US Billboard chart's top five since 2019 and has also collaborated with stars including Drake and J Cole on hit singles.

Supporters cheered outside a Los Angeles courthouse after the verdict, which came following three days of jury deliberations.

The 33-year-old faced five felony counts, including murder for hire resulting in death and conspiracy. If convicted, he could have faced a life sentence.

Although Banks was found not guilty of the charges in the case, he remains in custody and faces a separate trial on 5 October, where he will face racketeering murder and firearms charges.

"While we are disappointed with the jury's decision regarding Durk Banks, a.k.a. 'Lil Durk,' we look forward to presenting our evidence at his second trial", First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli said in a statement.

In the three-week trial, two co-defendants were tried alongside Banks. Deandre "OTF Dede" Wilson and David "Browneyez" Lindsey were convicted of stalking and conspiracy to commit stalking, but acquitted of murder-for-hire charges, the BBC's US partner CBS News reports .

The trial relied on three co-operating witnesses, Kavon "OTF Vonnie" Grant, Keith "Flacka" Jones and Kacey "OTF Jam" Hester, who reached plea deals and testified against Banks, Wilson and Lindsey.

It stemmed from a fatal shooting in August 2022 at a petrol station in Los Angeles, where a car carrying Rondo, whose real name is Tyquian Bowman, was shot at. Bowman was unharmed, but his cousin Saviay'a Robinson, who was also in the car, was killed.

Federal prosecutors accused Banks of plotting to kill Bowman, in retaliation for the earlier murder of Chicago OTF rapper King Von, who was signed to OTF. Von was killed in 2020 during an early-morning exchange of gunfire in Atlanta.

A friend of Bowman was charged with King Von's murder, but the charges were later dropped. Bowman was not arrested or charged.

Authorities said Banks made it known that he would "pay a bounty" to anyone who killed Bowman. Prosecutors argued that Banks felt pressure on social media to avenge Von's death.

Banks founded OTF in 2010. He won the 2024 Grammy Award for Best Melodic Rap Performance for his single "All My Life" featuring J Cole. He has also been nominated for a Grammy three other times.

articles.title: In 2008, wind turbines arrived in Iowa's Howard County; by 2024-25, 147 turbines generated $2.71 million in taxes and helped fund 30+ bridge projects and 20 miles of paving
articles.summary: US News: When wind turbines first appeared across Howard County in northeastern Iowa in 2008, they became part of the rural landscape. Nearly two decades later.
articles.body: When wind turbines first appeared across Howard County in northeastern Iowa in 2008, they became part of the rural landscape. Nearly two decades later, the towering structures have become something more than a source of renewable energy. For the county, wind power has also become a major source of public money, helping pay for bridges, roads, parks, conservation projects and local schools.A 2025 case study by the Centre for Rural Affairs found that Howard County had 147 wind turbines with a combined production capacity of 244 megawatts. In the 2024-25 tax year, the turbines generated $2.71 million in tax revenue, accounting for about 14.5% of the county's overall revenue.The money has been particularly significant for a rural county with a relatively small and declining population. Howard County had 9,469 residents in 2020, down from 9,566 in 2010, even as Iowa's overall population grew by about 5% during the same period. With limited population growth and a largely stagnant tax base, officials said the additional revenue from wind projects has helped the county maintain infrastructure without placing the same burden on residents.From wind farms to bridges and roadsThe first wind projects in Howard County were the Pioneer I and II developments, whose turbines were erected in 2008 and 2009. The projects installed 182 turbines, producing 178 MW of capacity, across the northwest corner of Howard County and the northeast corner of neighbouring Mitchell County.In 2019, Madison Gas and Electric added another 33 turbines, with 66 MW of capacity, around 12 miles west of Cresco, the Howard County seat. The Centre for Rural Affairs' county-level tally puts the number of turbines within Howard County at 147.The county used a financing mechanism known as Tax Increment Financing, or TIF, to channel much of the wind-related tax revenue into infrastructure and other public projects. TIF essentially allows governments to use increases in property-tax revenue associated with new development to finance community improvements. In Howard County, the system was used to fund $21.5 million worth of special projects without an additional cost to local residents, according to the case study. The largest share went into roads and bridges.Wind-related TIF money funded 30 bridge replacements involving bridges longer than 20 feet, a portion of four bridge rehabilitations and two smaller bridge replacements. Together, bridge projects received about $6.5 million. Another $12 million went toward roads, including 20 miles of paving and eight miles of grading.The Iowa Legislature's 2024-25 annual urban renewal report also shows that Howard County maintains a dedicated Wind Urban Renewal Area. The report says its purpose includes improvements to road shoulders, bridges, approaches, culverts and conservation projects in parks. It recorded $1.29 million in TIF revenue for the area during the fiscal year, with more than $1 million spent through the wind-farm TIF programme.‘We would have been forced to close’ bridgesThe impact is particularly visible in the county's bridge network. Howard County Engineer Nick Rissman told researchers that without the wind-turbine funding, officials would have faced difficult choices over which bridges to maintain.The additional money allowed the county to double the number of bridge projects it completed between 2010 and 2020 compared with the previous decade, according to the case study. More than 30 bridge projects were fully paid for through the wind-related funding without increasing taxes on residents.The benefit also extended beyond individual projects. About $1.5 million went toward equipment, including portions of the cost of six motor graders, a tractor with a mower and a dump truck.Rissman described the effect as a “snowball” process. By completing road projects earlier and purchasing equipment, the county could take on additional work instead of allowing roads to deteriorate until they required more expensive repairs.Parks, conservation and schools also benefitThe wind revenue did not stop at transportation infrastructure. The county allocated another $1.5 million to recreation and conservation projects. These included renovations at local parks, improvements at a nature centre, dam repairs, watershed projects and fishing habitat.Lake Hendricks Park, for example, received funding for fishing structures, watershed improvements and road paving. Money also went toward renovations at Florenceville Park, Lylah's Marsh Park, Vernon Springs Park and Lidtke Park, as well as improvements at the Bonair shooting range. The Prairie Springs and Wapsi Great Western Line recreational trails also received funding for repaving.Local schools have benefited as well. Wind projects provided an additional $228,071 annually to the Riceville Community School District and Howard-Winneshiek Community School District. The money can support school grounds and buildings, equipment and technology, transportation and other expenses.The wind development also contributes to the taxable property base of the school districts. The case study noted that Riceville's school district had the third-lowest total general tax rate among Iowa's 334 school districts, partly because of the high taxable valuation created by wind turbines.Farmers get another source of incomeThe financial impact is not limited to government coffers. Farmers who host turbines receive payments through land-lease agreements with wind-energy developers. Several Howard County landowners interviewed for the study said the additional income had helped them reinvest in their farms, including purchasing machinery, building sheds and improving their properties.The experience has not been without challenges. County officials said wind developers must take responsibility for damage caused to local roads during construction, while farmers stressed the importance of carefully negotiated lease agreements.Still, Howard County's experience offers a striking example of how a renewable-energy project can have effects far beyond electricity generation. The turbines standing in Iowa's fields are producing power, but their financial footprint can be seen elsewhere too: in newly paved roads, repaired bridges, upgraded parks, better-equipped schools and farm operations receiving another stream of income. For a rural county facing a limited tax base and little population growth, the wind has effectively become a source of infrastructure funding.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
